recorded.prompt:q-shift: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-shift: 'Values much smaller than s all look alike; values much larger than s keep their ratios.' In the C/D example the ratio goes from 3.162 to 1.006 at sh=10.
recorded.prompt:q-defaults: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-defaults: 'HiGHS... documented default mip_rel_gap is 10^-4... SCIP's documented limits/gap default is 0'. A benchmark on defaults would time HiGHS to 'within 0.01%' and SCIP to 'exactly'.

recorded.outcome:q-anecdote: 'compare settings pairwise on every instance and seed, report the ratio of shifted geometric means and the win/loss count, and treat any single pair as an anecdote.'

recorded.prompt:q-shift:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-shift:a: In the C/D case, D/C is 3.162 under the geometric mean and 1.006 with shift 10. The shift does change the ratio.
recorded.prompt:q-shift:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-shift:b: The analogous C/D case gives 1.006, not exactly 1. max(1,·) only keeps the logarithms nonnegative.
recorded.prompt:q-shift:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-shift:d: In the C/D case (tie on hard instances, D slower on easy ones), D/C stays above one at 1.006. It does not flip.
recorded.prompt:q-defaults:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-defaults:b: 'All three say OPTIMAL, but HiGHS stopped with its bound $5k above its plan... a gap of 0.0089% counts as optimal for HiGHS.'
recorded.prompt:q-defaults:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-defaults:c: The page runs them 'with no gap target set (each solver's own default), through MathOpt'. MathOpt does not override the defaults.
recorded.prompt:q-defaults:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-defaults:d: 'The gap's formula differs too: HiGHS divides by its primal bound, SCIP by the smaller of the two values.'
recorded.prompt:q-anecdote:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-anecdote:a: 'treat any single pair as an anecdote'. Cells also repeat exactly, so a rerun of the same seed would only repeat the same number.
recorded.prompt:q-anecdote:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-anecdote:b: Running only the same instance remains a single anecdote ('treat any single pair as an anecdote'). The harness also fixes one thread.
recorded.prompt:q-anecdote:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-anecdote:c: Within one solver 'a deterministic unit is a fair yardstick'. A single instance is still an anecdote.
